title: Subdivision 124-M roll-over — scrip for scrip (exchange of shares or units)
summary: Scrip for scrip CGT roll-over for company takeovers and similar arrangements: post-CGT shares (or options) in one company are exchanged for shares in another, or units in one trust for units in another. Requires a single arrangement resulting in 80%+ ownership (or a takeover bid / scheme of arrangement), post-CGT acquisition, a gain would otherwise arise, and a choice (jointly with the replacement entity in some cases). The gain is disregarded and the cost base carries into the replacement interest; partial roll-over applies where cash or other proceeds are included. Subsection coverage: operative 124-775 (guide), 124-780(1)-(7), 124-781(1)-(6), 124-782(1)-(4), 124-785(1)-(4), 124-790(1)-(2), 124-795(1)-(4), 124-800(1)-(2), 124-810(1)-(6) mapped to nodes; 124-780(6)-(7), 124-781(5)-(6), 124-810(1)-(6) (machinery definitions); 124-795(3) (cross-ref transitional).

nodes.label: An entity holds post-CGT shares in a company, or units in a trust, and exchanges them for shares or units in another entity
nodes.body: Subdivision 124-M (scrip for scrip) allows a roll-over where post-CGT shares or trust interests are replaced with other shares or trust interests — for example, in a company takeover (s 124-775). The gain is deferred into the replacement interest.

nodes.label: Does the exchange involve a CGT event that would otherwise crystallise a gain (A1 / E1 / E2)?
nodes.body: The roll-over under this Subdivision interacts with: CGT event A1 (s 104-10) — disposal of your original shares or units — which would otherwise give rise to a capital gain; and CGT events E1 (creating a trust over property) and E2 (transferring property to a trust) for trust unit exchanges. Where no CGT event arises, no roll-over is needed. Section 104-230 (CGT event K6) may also apply where pre-CGT shares in a company are exchanged for shares in the replacement entity, potentially disregarding a gain under the roll-over (s 124-800(2)).

nodes.label: You exchange your original interest for a replacement interest in another company or trust
nodes.body: The exchange must be: a share in the original company for a share in another company, or an option/right/similar interest issued by the original entity for a similar interest in another company (s 124-780(1)(a)). Options cannot be exchanged for shares (and vice versa). Trust interests are covered by s 124-781: units or other interests in a trust exchanged for units in another trust, where entities have fixed entitlements to all of the income and capital of both trusts.

nodes.label: Is the exchange in consequence of a single arrangement that results in 80%+ ownership of voting shares (s 124-780(2)(a))? (A compliant takeover bid or court-approved Part 5.1 arrangement under s 124-780(2A) must also satisfy the 80% test)
nodes.body:
The arrangement must satisfy s 124-780(2)(a): an acquiring entity (not a member of a wholly-owned group) becomes the owner of 80% or more of the voting shares in the original entity, or a member of such a group increases its percentage. All owners of voting shares (except the acquiring company) must be able to participate (s 124-780(2)(b)), and participation must be on substantially the same terms for all owners of interests of a particular type (s 124-780(2)(c)).

Alternatively, under s 124-780(2A), the arrangement must satisfy paragraph (2)(a) (the 80%+ test) AND be one or more of:
• a takeover bid under the Corporations Act 2001 not carried out in contravention of the provisions mentioned in s 612(a)-(g) of that Act; or
• a compromise or arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act 2001 approved by court order for the purposes of paragraph 411(4)(b) of that Act.

IMPORTANT: The 80%+ ownership test in s 124-780(2)(a) is always required — the takeover bid or scheme of arrangement is an additional qualifier, not a substitute.

nodes.label: Are the roll-over conditions (a)-(d) met? (post-CGT acquisition, gain would arise, replacement entity, choice)
nodes.body:
The conditions (s 124-780(3)(a)-(d)): (a) You acquired the original interest on or after 20 September 1985; (b) Apart from the roll-over, you would make a capital gain from a CGT event in relation to it; (c) The replacement interest is in the acquiring entity or the ultimate holding company of the wholly-owned group; (d) You choose the roll-over (jointly with the replacement entity where s 124-782 applies).

Conditions (e) and (f) are checked separately in the next step.

nodes.label: If you and the acquiring entity did not deal at arm's length: are the additional conditions met?
nodes.body:
Where the parties did not deal at arm's length and either:
(a) Neither the original entity nor the replacement entity had at least 300 members (or beneficiaries for trusts) just before the arrangement started; or
(b) The original interest holder, the original entity AND an acquiring entity were all members of the same linked group just before that time (s 124-780(4)(b)).

The additional conditions (s 124-780(5)) are:
• The market value of your capital proceeds for the exchange is at least substantially the same as the market value of your original interest; and
• Your replacement interest carries the same kind of rights and obligations as those attached to your original interest.

Note: The three entities in s 124-780(4)(b) are: the original interest holder, the original entity, and an acquiring entity. Section 124-810 deals with when a company or trust is not regarded as having 300 members/beneficiaries.

nodes.label: Do any of the exceptions in s 124-795 apply?
nodes.body:
You cannot obtain the roll-over if any exception in s 124-795 applies:
(1) You are a *foreign resident* just before you stop owning the original interest, unless the replacement interest is *taxable Australian property* just after you acquire it.
(2) Any capital gain from the replacement interest would be disregarded (except because of another roll-over), or you and the acquiring entity are in the same *wholly-owned group* and the acquiring entity is a foreign resident.
(3) You can choose a roll-over under *Division 122* (disposal to wholly-owned company) or *Division 615* (business restructure) for the same CGT event.
(4) The replacement entity makes a choice to exclude you from the roll-over under this subsection, and notifies you in writing before the exchange.

nodes.label: Make the roll-over choice (election under s 103-25; jointly with replacement entity where s 124-782 applies)
nodes.body:
The choice is the election to obtain the roll-over, made under s 103-25. This is a separate step from the eligibility conditions tested above.

Where s 124-782 applies (you are a significant stakeholder or common stakeholder for the arrangement), you and the replacement entity must jointly choose, and you must inform the replacement entity in writing of the cost base of your original interest just before the CGT event. The acquiring entity then takes over the cost base (s 124-782(1)) or, for cancelled interests, the cost base is reasonably allocated to the new interests (s 124-782(2)-(4)).

If you do not choose the roll-over, the exchange is taxed as a normal CGT event A1.

nodes.label: Do your capital proceeds include something other than the replacement interest?
nodes.body: If the capital proceeds include ineligible proceeds (something other than the replacement interest), you can obtain only a partial roll-over: there is no roll-over for the ineligible part of the original interest (s 124-790(1)). The cost base of the ineligible part is the part of the original cost base reasonably attributable to it (s 124-790(2)).

nodes.label: Roll-over applies: gain disregarded; replacement's cost base = reasonably attributed cost base of the original
nodes.body: The capital gain from your original interest is disregarded (s 124-785(1)). The first element of the cost base of each asset received is worked out by reasonably attributing the cost base of the original interest for which it was exchanged (s 124-785(2)), reduced by so much as is attributable to an ineligible part (s 124-785(3)). The first element of the reduced cost base is worked out similarly (s 124-785(4)).

nodes.label: Partial roll-over: the ineligible part is taxed, the rest defers
nodes.body: There is no roll-over for the ineligible part of the original interest — you make a capital gain on that part based on its cost base (s 124-790). The eligible part follows the normal roll-over consequences.

nodes.label: Pre-CGT interests exchanged: replacement's cost base is market value, reduced for K6 gain disregarded (s 124-800 anti-avoidance)
nodes.body: If you exchange an interest acquired before 20 September 1985, the first element of the cost base and reduced cost base of the replacement interest is its market value just after you acquired it (s 124-800(1)). The cost base is further reduced by the amount of any capital gain from CGT event K6 (s 104-230) that is disregarded under subsection 104-230(10), because that subsection defers gain that would otherwise be recognised under K6 where the roll-over is available (s 124-800(2) — anti-avoidance preventing double benefit).

nodes.label: Scrip for scrip roll-over applied — gain deferred into the replacement interest
nodes.body: The gain on the original interest is disregarded and the cost base carries into the replacement interest, so tax is deferred until the replacement is disposed of.

nodes.label: No roll-over — the exchange is a normal CGT event
nodes.body: If the arrangement, conditions, additional conditions or exceptions fail, the exchange of shares or units is taxed as a disposal of the original interest under the usual CGT rules (CGT event A1).

nodes.label: Was the original interest acquired before 20 September 1985 (pre-CGT)?
nodes.body: Section 124-780(3)(a) requires the original interest to be acquired on or after 20 September 1985. If the interest was acquired before that date (pre-CGT), the roll-over under s 124-780 does not apply to that interest. Instead, the cost base of the replacement interest is its market value just after acquisition, reduced by any K6 gain disregarded under s 124-800(2). CGT event K6 (s 104-230) may apply to pre-CGT shares in a company exchanged for replacement shares.

nodes.label: Is the interest a Chess Unit of Foreign Security (CUFS)?
nodes.body: Under s 124-780(6), this section applies to the holder of a Chess Unit of Foreign Security as if the holder held the underlying interests that the unit represents. A CUFS is an interest, traded on the stock market operated by ASX Limited, in a foreign share, unit or interest. If the interest is a CUFS, the roll-over analysis proceeds by treating the holder as holding the underlying shares/interests directly.

nodes.label: Are the additional conditions in s 124-780(3)(e)-(f) satisfied? (written notification of cost base; no additional equity/debt to non-members)
nodes.body:
Section 124-780(3) contains six conditions. In addition to the conditions checked previously (post-CGT acquisition, gain, replacement entity, choice), paragraphs (e) and (f) also must be satisfied:

(e) If s 124-782 applies (the holder is a significant stakeholder or common stakeholder), the original interest holder must inform the replacement entity in writing of the cost base of its original interest worked out just before the CGT event happened in relation to it.

(f) If an acquiring entity is a member of a wholly-owned group, no member of the group may issue equity (other than a replacement interest), or owe new debt, under the arrangement to an entity that is not a member of the group in relation to the issuing of the replacement interest.

nodes.label: For trust unit exchanges: does the arrangement satisfy s 124-781(2) conditions? (80%+ trust voting interests, participation, same terms)
nodes.body:
Where the exchange involves trust interests (units or options/rights in a trust), s 124-781 applies instead of s 124-780 for the arrangement conditions. Under s 124-781(1)(b), entities must have fixed entitlements to all of the income and capital of both the original trust and the acquiring trust.

Section 124-781(2) requires the arrangement to:
(a) Result in the acquiring entity owning 80% or more of the trust voting interests in the original entity, or if none, 80% or more of the units or other interests; (b) Allow at least all owners of trust voting interests (or units/other interests) in the original entity (except the acquiring entity) to participate; (c) Make participation available on substantially the same terms for all owners of interests of a particular type.

Section 124-781(2A) provides an alternative for takeover bids (without the Part 5.1 compromise option available for shares under s 124-780(2A)).

nodes.label: For trust unit exchanges: are the s 124-781(3) conditions met? (post-CGT, gain, choice, written notification)
Does the exchange involve trust interests or shares?
nodes.body: The scrip for scrip roll-over covers both company shares (s 124-780) and trust interests (s 124-781). Different conditions apply to each. If the exchange involves trust interests, the s 124-781 requirements must be satisfied. If the exchange involves shares, the s 124-780 requirements apply.
